title: Earth's Day Was 1.66 Milliseconds Shorter
hook: Earth recorded a day 1.66 milliseconds shorter than normal.
closing: Tiny timing shifts matter because global systems depend on clocks matching Earth's rotation.
question: Could you notice a shorter day?

segments.say: A 2024 day ran 1.66 milliseconds short, setting Earth's latest timing record.
Since 1972, clocks added 27 leap seconds and removed none, because Earth usually lagged.
By 2035, a negative leap second has a 40 percent chance, reversing the old correction.
